title: Christiane Torloni opens up about the pain of losing her son and her new chapter
seoTitle: Christiane Torloni on losing her son & her new chapter
subtitle: The actress addresses loss, new beginnings, and reflections on life as she approaches 70
excerpt: Christiane Torloni recalls the 1991 death of her son Guilherme, discusses her stage career, and talks about taking up surfing as she approaches 70.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Christiane Torloni opened up about her life journey, speaking on loss, new beginnings, and the different ways she found to keep living after a period of silence regarding the death of her son, Guilherme. The actress, who is about to turn 70, recalled the 1991 accident and the daily process of rebuilding her own existence in the face of a pain that never fully fades.

Losing her son and rebuilding her life

Guilherme's death occurred in 1991 at the age of 12, following a car accident in the garage of the actress's own home. Christiane described the tragedy as a mother's ultimate test, stating that life itself was at stake at that moment.

More than three decades later, she explains that finding a reason to live required daily effort. Rebuilding this path is described by her as an immense task that never truly ends, demanding a daily renewal of the choice to keep living.

Support and affection in difficult times

At the time of the tragedy, the actress relied on outpourings of support from loved ones and strangers alike. Letters and messages sent by those who followed her grief proved vital in keeping her from giving up during a period considered highly critical.

Current stage work and career

Currently, Christiane is performing in Rio de Janeiro in the play Dois de Nós, written by Gustavo Pinheiro and directed by José Possi Neto. The cast features Antonio Fagundes, one of the actress's close friends.

Her personal experience with emotionally heavy characters fosters a deep connection with the story presented on stage. Alongside the play's run, she continues to build her career across television, theater, and film.

New discoveries and confronting ageism

As she approaches 70, Christiane has found a new activity: surfing. The sport, which her mother forbade when she was younger, has turned into an experience of tranquility and focus on the present moment.

The actress also reflects on ageism, defining age-based prejudice as cruel because it makes people doubt others' capabilities. She argues that aging brings new discoveries and that the passage of time does not mean loss in every area of life.

With information from Terra.
